text:
Jimmy Snuggerud has 10 goals in 21 games, and the Minneapolis kid is the most dangerous finisher the Blues have had this fall. Part of that is real. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 7.7 scoring chances per 60 from the home-plate area last season, 96th percentile among forwards, and he likes to work from behind the net, where 29% of his setups start against 8% for a typical forward.

Part of it won't last. He's scoring on 22% of his shots against 12% last season, with 10 goals on 5.9 expected. Our range puts his true shooting closer to 14%, which is still good. The last ten games already look more normal: four goals, seven points, right on what we'd expect at his ice time.

Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.3 wins last season, nearly all from offense, with the cost at the other end (opponents got more chances with him on, bottom 7% of forwards). That's the trade-off to watch: a 22-year-old who scores, at about 18 minutes a night, still learning what to do without the puck.
